world.bio: Founder and director of Scarborough Keys & Strings, a non-profit community music school in a former bank branch on Kingston Road. We teach about 140 kids a week, most on sliding-scale fees, plus a seniors' singing circle on Thursday mornings. I trained as a cellist, did a decade of freelancing, then ended up writing grants at midnight. I have six-year-old twins who just started kindergarten, I play bass in a Sunday cover band, and I'm currently in a dispute with the landlord about the school's heating.
skills_assets: A non-profit community music school in Scarborough, with 140 students and 11 part-time teachers
A former bank branch: the vault now holds the drum kit and the stacked chairs
Two small practice rooms with digital keyboards, one larger room with a drum kit and amps
Relationships with the TDSB music coordinator, two churches that lend us halls for recitals, and a local credit union that sponsors our spring concert
A cello, a bass, and a regular Sunday night cover band called The Overdrafts

projects.name: Fall grant cycle
projects.text: Three applications out: Ontario Arts Council, a municipal community grant, and a family foundation. Due dates are 15 October, 31 October and 14 November. I write after the twins are asleep, usually 10pm to 1am. The OAC one asks for 'measurable outcomes' and I keep writing sentences that sound like a slide deck.

projects.name: Piano programme
projects.text: We have a waitlist of 30 kids for piano lessons. We have two practice rooms and both have digital keyboards with weighted keys, which are not the same as an acoustic piano, as the teachers keep reminding me. A decent acoustic upright new costs about $6,000 CAD; a used one in good condition around $2,500, and the school's entire equipment budget this year is $3,800 including strings, reeds and repairs. I've priced it a hundred times.

projects.name: Heating dispute
projects.text: The landlord says the heating is 'adequate'. Our kids' fingers are cold in January. I've documented temperatures in the main room for a month. Lowest was 14 degrees.

notes.text: School's second week. Forty-two kids turned up on Saturday, which is a record for September. A new family of three siblings from Eritrea came in; the youngest saw the keyboards and went straight to them. Teacher Marcus said he's already got an ear. But the waitlist for piano is now thirty. I looked at the list on my phone in the car for ten minutes.

Midnight. OAC grant draft. 'Describe the impact of your programming on the community.' I've written the same paragraph eleven times. Finally typed: 'Our school is where kids who can't afford lessons learn to love music.' Deleted it. Typed it again. Left it.
Twins' first full week of kindergarten. Ravi cried at drop-off. Anika didn't. Both said school was 'fine'. Husband Sam took them in today so I could go to the school early and fix a leaking radiator.

Rehearsal with the Overdrafts. We're playing a wedding in November. Our drummer Gaurav keeps rushing the second verse of 'Superstition'. I told him we can't all be Stevie Wonder. He said 'I'm not rushing, you're dragging'. Our guitarist took his side. Loneliness of the bassist.

Heating dispute: the landlord's rep came and said it's 'within code'. I showed him the temperature logs. He said logs aren't evidence. I said they are if you're a small non-profit with no lawyer. He didn't appreciate that.

Seniors' circle on Thursday. Mrs Chen sang 'Edelweiss' with her eyes closed and everyone went quiet. Afterwards she told me she hadn't sung in public since she left Hong Kong forty years ago. I said you sang beautifully. She said 'the old piano at the church was better'. I wrote that on my hand.

Spoke to Marcus about piano. He said the kids learn finger technique on the digital but when they go home to someone's grandmother's piano, they can't hear the difference in touch. Parents are noticing too. I need an acoustic.

Looked up used pianos on Kijiji. A Yamaha U1 for $2,800 in Markham, but you have to move it yourself and pay a tuner. Moving alone is $400. Tuning, $150. And the board hasn't approved any spending above $500 without a vote.
Gaurav's ex turned up at the Sunday gig and he played the whole set sixteen bars too fast. We drove home in silence. Then he said sorry. I said it's fine. We've all been there.
Called the credit union about the spring concert sponsorship; they want a letter. Writing another letter. I've become a person who thinks in bullet points.

messages.text:
Marcus: 30 on the waitlist now. Parents are asking.
Priya: I know. I'm working on it.
Marcus: Can we at least have a better keyboard?
Priya: The budget's tight, but I'll see.

Sam: Ravi wants to bring his cello to school.
Priya: Tell him it's too big.
Sam: He cried.
Priya: Okay, bring it Friday for show and tell.

Davies: The building meets code. No further action required.
Priya: Can we get that in writing?
Davies: I'll send a note.
Priya: Thank you.

Lena: Is the piano proposal ready for the October meeting?
Priya: I'll prepare options.
Lena: Be realistic. We don't have much.

Tom: We're happy to sponsor the concert again at $2,000.
Priya: That's wonderful.
Tom: Can you send a one-page summary of last year's attendance?
Priya: Yes.
